entries.def: a noun which has no plural form and isn't used with the indefinite article
entries.example: e.g. Can you send me some information? (NOT an information or informations)

entries.def: a noun which only has a plural form and isn't used with the indefinite article
entries.example: e.g. He was wearing blue trousers and a white shirt. (NOT a blue trouser)

entries.def: the base form of a verb
entries.example: e.g. We decided to stop for lunch.
e.g. wake up, turn sth on, look after sth/sb.

entries.def: a group of words with a meaning that is different from the individual words
entries.example: e.g. never mind, keep an eye on sth, etc.

entries.def: a verb which needs a direct object
entries.example: e.g. The police caught the man ['the man' is the direct object of the verb 'caught'].

entries.def: A verb which doesn't need a direct object is intransitive
entries.example: e.g. Tim and his brother are always arguing.

entries.def: a word or phrase which is informal is used mostly in spoken English. Formal English is more common in writing or with people you don't know very well.

entries.example: e.g. 'big' and 'large' are synonyms in many contexts.

entries.def: Dictionaries show the pronunciation of a word using phonemic symbols
entries.example: e.g. book /buk/, before /bɪ'fɔ:/, cinema /'sɪnəmə/, and so on.
Hyphens are used to connect certain words or parts of a word together, e.g. a ten-year-old child.
